key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines optical, electrical, and barrier functions to boost both efficiency and environmental stability in Schottky solar cells.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical low-cost interface stack for silicon photovoltaics that improves charge collection while protecting hygroscopic organic layers from ambient degradation.
method: Benchmark trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si against Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS as an anti-reflection coating, mild p-type dopant for graphene, and conductivity enhancer.
Leverage graphene as both a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer device reached 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for Gr/n-Si, and retained about 90% of initial efficiency after 75 days in ambient conditions, compared with ~29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: Performance and stability gains were shown on untextured substrates, so scaling to textured or large-area manufacturing may change the optical and interfacial balance.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
